questions.question: When Allah granted Luqman wisdom, what was the very first instruction that accompanied that gift?
options: A) Establish the daily prayers
B) Be grateful to Allah
C) Teach your son about tawhid
D) Avoid idle speech and amusement
questions.explanation: Verse 12 records that Luqman was given hikmah and immediately commanded 'Be grateful to Allah.' The tafsir notes a profound connection: a truly wise person recognizes that every blessing comes from Allah alone, and this recognition — when it moves from mind to heart to action — is genuine gratitude.

questions.question: True or false: The scholarly consensus among classical Sunni scholars, including Ibn Kathir and Imam al-Tabari, is that Luqman was a prophet.
questions.explanation: The majority of the Salaf, including Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn al-Musayyib, held that Luqman was not a prophet but a righteous man — originally of Nubian or Ethiopian origin — whom Allah distinguished with wisdom. Ibn Kathir affirms this as the scholarly consensus in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim.

questions.question: Luqman describes associating partners with Allah as 'zulm azeem.' What does the word 'zulm' primarily mean in Arabic?
options: A) Disobedience to parents
B) Injustice — placing something where it does not belong
C) A grave sin requiring a specific expiation
D) Ingratitude toward one's benefactor
questions.explanation: The tafsir explains that zulm means injustice — specifically, placing something where it does not belong. Worshipping anything other than the Creator is the ultimate misplacement: directing to a created thing the reverence that belongs solely to the One who brought it into existence. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi notes that shirk is uniquely self-defeating since the very beings worshipped derive their power entirely from Allah.

questions.question: True or false: The phrase 'min azm al-umur' at the end of verse 17 means that prayer, enjoining good, forbidding evil, and patience are optional acts of distinction rather than weighty obligations.
questions.explanation: Imam al-Qurtubi in Al-Jami li-Ahkam al-Quran confirms that 'azm al-umur' refers to matters of supreme importance that require firm resolve — these are among the weightiest obligations entrusted to believers, not optional extras. Luqman's inclusion of patience immediately after shows his awareness that moral engagement invites opposition.

questions.question: Which prominent Companion did Ibn Kathir cite as interpreting 'lahw al-hadith' specifically as singing — and reportedly gave this answer three times for emphasis?
options: A) Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
B) Umar ibn al-Khattab
C) Ibn Masud
D) Abu Hurairah
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir records that when Ibn Masud was asked about the meaning of 'lahw al-hadith,' he replied emphatically three times that it refers to singing. Ibn Abbas, Jabir ibn Abd Allah, Mujahid, and Ikrimah shared similar interpretations. Imam Tabari concludes the verse encompasses all speech or amusement that diverts a person from Allah's path.

questions.question: Which Companion did Ibn Kathir report as the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) for verse 15, after his mother threatened to starve herself to pressure him into renouncing Islam?
options: A) Bilal ibn Rabah
B) Saad ibn Abi Waqqas
C) Ammar ibn Yasir
D) Khabbab ibn al-Aratt
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir references a narration recorded by al-Tabarani in which Saad ibn Abi Waqqas stated these verses concerned his situation. His mother swore to neither eat nor drink until he renounced the faith; Saad refused, and the verse was revealed vindicating his position: refuse shirk, yet accompany parents with kindness.

questions.question: True or false: Imam al-Tabari reports that verse 27 — about trees as pens and oceans as ink — may have been revealed in response to a challenge from Jewish scholars who argued a verse about human knowledge contradicted the Quran's claims.
questions.explanation: Imam Tabari records a reported context (sabab al-nuzul) in which Jewish scholars in Madinah cited a verse about limited human knowledge as a challenge. This verse was revealed to affirm that even all revealed knowledge combined is a negligible fraction of Allah's infinite knowledge. Ibn Kathir cross-references a parallel image in Surah al-Kahf (18:109).

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli explains why Luqman places prayer before enjoining good and forbidding evil in verse 17. What is that reason according to Al-Tafsir al-Munir?
options: A) Prayer is the easiest command and should precede harder ones
B) Prayer is the spiritual root that powers the moral courage needed for da'wah and social engagement
C) Prayer takes priority because it is the only purely individual obligation in the list
D) Prayer was the first pillar revealed, so it comes first in all counsel
questions.explanation: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir explains that a Muslim who has not established his relationship with Allah through prayer cannot sustain the moral courage needed for commanding good and forbidding evil. Prayer is the spiritual root system; da'wah is the branches; and patience is what allows the whole tree to withstand the storms of adversity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the five categories of exclusive divine knowledge ('mafatih al-ghayb') enumerated in verse 34?
options: A) The precise time of the Day of Judgment
B) What any soul will earn tomorrow
C) The names of those destined for Paradise
D) The land in which any soul will die
questions.explanation: The five categories in verse 34 are: knowledge of the Hour, the sending of rain, what is in the wombs, what a soul will earn tomorrow, and the land in which any soul will die. A hadith recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim confirms all five through the Prophet's own words.

questions.question: True or false: Wahbah al-Zuhayli argues that modern medical ultrasound technology has effectively superseded the Quranic assertion that knowledge of what is in the womb belongs exclusively to Allah.
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli clarifies that these five categories refer to their complete, certain dimensions which remain with Allah alone. An ultrasound reveals biological data; Allah's knowledge encompasses the soul, its destiny, its faith, and every dimension of its existence — infinitely beyond what any technology can access. Probabilistic approximation is not divine certainty.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb observed a specific pedagogical reason why Luqman begins his counsel with the prohibition of shirk rather than with ritual practice. What is that reason according to Fi Zilal al-Quran?
options: A) Shirk is the easiest concept for children to grasp and should be addressed first
B) Correct theology must precede correct practice, because actions derive their spiritual validity from the worldview behind them
C) The Arab audience of Mecca was primarily guilty of shirk, making it the most urgent rebuke
D) Ritual commands can only be given after a formal declaration of faith
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb in Fi Zilal al-Quran argues that the Quran's pedagogical order here is deliberate: correct theology must precede correct practice because actions derive their spiritual validity from the intention and worldview behind them. A prayer offered from a confused theology is not the same as one offered from clarity of tawhid.

questions.question: In verse 16, Luqman tells his son that even a mustard-seed's weight of deed hidden in a rock will be brought forth by Allah. Which pair of divine names closes this verse?
options: A) Al-Alim (All-Knowing) and Al-Qadir (All-Powerful)
B) Al-Haqq (The Truth) and Al-Mubin (The Clear)
C) Al-Latif (Subtle) and Al-Khabir (All-Aware)
D) Al-Sami (All-Hearing) and Al-Basir (All-Seeing)
questions.explanation: The verse closes with Al-Latif (subtle, reaching hidden places) and Al-Khabir (acquainted with all details). These names, discussed in the layer 1 and layer 2 tafsir, affirm that Allah's awareness penetrates the smallest and most concealed realities — the theological foundation for the taqwa Luqman seeks to build in his son.
